thread:
priya: Heads up — onboarding pipeline started failing after last night's RBAC push. New hires hit errors on SCIM CreateUser for 3 orgs. 500s and retries. Anyone else seeing this?

josh: saw one alert earlier, but assumed transient backpressure. Can you paste the failing log snippet?

priya: paste: ```ERROR scim/provisioner: createUser failed org=acme-corp err=500 reason=decrypt_failed detail={"kms_error":"Decrypt failed: invalid ciphertext"} trace=...```

elaine: that's the KMS decrypt error we've seen when the org key alias was rotated but old ciphertext wasn't rewrapped. Which RBAC change did we push? that shouldn't touch KMS aliases.

priya: RBAC change was only policy layer (role -> group mapping) but infra had a small key rotation window yesterday (manual rotation by sec ops at 02:12 UTC). Not sure about sequence.

samir: quick theory: SCIM provisioning stores an encrypted external_id/identity fingerprint in metadata for dedupe. If decrypt fails, provisioner treats as collision or unknown state and throws 500. Need to check audit log for which service attempted decrypt and what key id used.

priya: grabbing audit. ```kms.audit: time=2026-03-19T02:12:35Z action=Decrypt key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/old-alias used_by=scim-provisioner request_id=abc123 result=AccessDenied``` Also saw later `KeyNotFound` in a few entries.

josh: AccessDenied vs KeyNotFound suggests a rekey/alias switch and the provisioner role lost permission on the new key or service principal changed. Did the RBAC change alter the IAM role used by the provisioner?

elaine: RBAC change should be only app-level; didn't touch the IAM role. But there was a terraform apply in infra at 02:15 that updated kms:Grant for service accounts — checking PR.

samir: if terraform removed old grants before re-adding for new key, there could be a short window where decrypts fail and SCIM queue accumulates. We should confirm queue backlog and whether failed messages retried idempotently.

priya: backlog looks substantial: provisioner logs show `RetryCount` up to 7 and exponential backoff. Some orgs hit duplicate-detection failures after retries ended.

infra-bot: deploy 1767 finished at 2026-03-19T02:14:00Z by elaine. Resources changed: aws_kms_key.rotation_enabled=true, aws_kms_grant.provisioner -> recreated.

josh: OK. Action plan: 1) Pause new SCIM jobs for affected orgs, 2) Validate KMS grants for the provisioner role, 3) Re-run decrypt probe against stored ciphertext using both old and new key ARNs (if we have wrapping material), 4) Backfill failed items after confirming decryption. Anyone want to pick steps 1/2?

elaine: I'll revert the grant recreation if we confirm it's the culprit. Running `aws kms list-grants --key-id <new-key>` and check granteePrincipal for provisioner role.

priya: I can pause queues for the three affected orgs now: acme-corp, nova-labs, helios-inc. Pausing means new hires will wait but no more 500 noise.

samir: also add a short-term guard in provisioner: if KMS decrypt fails with KeyNotFound/AccessDenied, surface a 409-ish retryable error instead of 500 to avoid downstream duplicate logic. We'll follow up with a code PR.

priya: paused. confirmations: ```provisioner> pause org=acme-corp -> ok
provisioner> pause org=nova-labs -> ok
provisioner> pause org=helios-inc -> ok```

josh: I checked grants: new-key has grant but granteePrincipal shows `arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/provisioner-legacy`. Our provisioner pod now runs as `provisioner-new` due to the RBAC mapping change. So grant is scoped to old principal.

elaine: that matches the timing: RBAC role rename occurred in the same change that updated app-level role mapping. Terraform recreated grant but with the principal value derived from the pre-change state variable. Classic race.

samir: two immediate fixes: A) add grant for `provisioner-new` principal so decrypts succeed, B) consider switching provisioner to use KMS key policy that references a role tag or allow sts:AssumeRole for both principals to avoid fragile naming. Which is faster?

elaine: I'll create an emergency grant for `provisioner-new` (fast). Then follow with a patch to key policy to be role-agnostic tomorrow. Applying now.

infra-bot: create-grant request submitted by elaine at 2026-03-19T03:05:42Z -> grant-id=gr-0a1b2c applied to key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/new-alias

priya: re-running failed decrypt probe against one sample user now...```curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROV_TOKEN" https://provisioner.internal/ops/decrypt-probe?ct=abc123``` returned 200 and decrypted payload. Nice.

josh: great. Start a controlled replay of the backlog for acme-corp only (small) and watch audit logs / retry behavior. Keep queues paused for the other two until green.

priya: replay started for acme-corp — monitoring. Initial batch 20 users — 18 succeeded, 2 failed due to validation for email duplicates (expected). No 500s.

samir: follow-up recommendations for postmortem: - tighten IaC ordering so KMS grants are created before role renames are applied; - add canary test in deploy pipeline that runs a decrypt-probe against sample ciphertext after key rotation; - update provisioner to classify KMS decrypt errors more granularly and avoid 500 paths that trigger dedupe divergence; - add audit alert when decrypt error rate > 1% for a minute.

priya: noted. I'll create the incident doc and assign owners. Quick question: do we need to rewrap any stored ciphertexts generated under the old key? or is grant approach enough?

elaine: grant approach is sufficient for now. But long-term rewrapping (re-encryption with new key) is cleaner to retire the old key. We'll include a rewrap/backfill plan in the postmortem. Might do it org-by-org to avoid big batch windows.

security: please ensure this is logged as a KMS-related incident and that we capture the exact terraform diff. add SLO blameless notes.

oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-1431 category=identity impact=medium owner=priya viewers=eng-security,infra,prod-eng

priya: thanks all. I'll keep the convo updated in the incident doc and start the postmortem skeleton. If anyone needs more log snippets or grant ids, ping me. :thumbsup:
